title: In Space, Candle Flames Are Round
hook: Light a candle in space, and the flame turns into a ball instead of rising up
summary: In space, hot air doesn't rise, so a candle flame burns round and blue.

text: A candle flame always rises up to a point.
It's so obvious you've probably never wondered why.
The hot air around the flame is light, so it rises.
Cooler air from below flows in to fill the gap.
This flow pulls the flame up into a long, thin shape.

panels.text: So what about in space, where nothing has weight?

text: This is a candle lit on the space station.
so the flame spreads out into a round shape.
On Earth, soot rises, so the top of the flame looks yellow.
In space, the flame is bluer and burns better.
On the space station, they also run experiments that set drops of fuel on fire.
Once lit, the flame burns like a ball wrapped around the drop.

panels.text: Guess birthday cake candles would be round in space too
